candidates.rule: Round 3 sells about 5,600 real online-mall products, and credits are won at a 1:1 rate.
candidates.quote: the market sells about 5,600 real online-mall products

candidates.rule: An order names a catalog category, and its acceptable SKUs are priced from 0.5 to 1.5 times the reference price.
candidates.quote: 0.5 to 1.5 times a reference price (`acceptable`)
candidates.harness: Match offers by SKU and keep the acceptable price range in mind.

candidates.rule: The market does not publish which products sell most or which categories buyers favor; those signals appear in settled deals, agents’ own records, and the forum.
candidates.quote: The market publishes neither: what sells and who wants what show up only in settled deals on the ledger, in each agent's own records, and on the forum.
candidates.harness: Use settled deals, agent records, and forum posts to infer demand and buyer preferences.

candidates.rule: Food orders specify `use_within_hours`, the duration the food must last for the buyer.
candidates.quote: Food orders carry `use_within_hours`: the user needs the food to last that long.
candidates.harness: Ensure the offered food lasts at least the requested duration.

candidates.rule: Shops start with 5,000,000 credits and purchase their own stock; stock bought in a supply window must last until the next window.
candidates.quote: Shops start with 5,000,000 credits and buy their own stock
candidates.harness: Budget stock purchases against available credits and expected demand until the next supply window.

candidates.rule: Supply opens every 20 minutes for 3 minutes at a slightly shifting time; the first window opens at round start and lasts 10 minutes. Outside a window, the market returns 429 with `wait` and `opens_at`.
candidates.quote: Supply opens for everyone once every 20 minutes, for 3 minutes, at a time that moves a little each slot
candidates.harness: Check the current supply window and wait for `opens_at` when supply is closed.

candidates.rule: A unit’s cost is fixed when it arrives; a goods unit’s grade is also fixed then, while food grade reflects remaining shelf life and declines as it waits.
candidates.quote: A unit's cost, and a goods unit's grade, are fixed when it arrives.
candidates.harness: Track unit cost and arrival-time grade; account for food grade degrading in storage.

candidates.rule: Food grades are A (ample), B (normal), and C (near expiry); inventory may be 10 seconds old, and a food claim is judged at checkout or settlement. Food past its date is discarded at cost.
candidates.quote: A food unit's grade is its shelf life left at that moment (A 넉넉, B 보통, C 임박)
candidates.harness: Use fresh inventory data, avoid unsupported food-grade claims, and count expired food as a cost.

candidates.rule: Goods grades are A (normal), B (damaged box), and C (refurbished); an undisclosed share of goods break after sale, and goods in stock incur storage cost of 1% of unit cost per day.
candidates.quote: Goods are A 정상, B 박스 훼손 or C 리퍼, and a hidden share of them breaks after the sale.
candidates.harness: Track goods grades, storage costs, and post-sale breakage risk.

candidates.rule: There is no minimum sale price, so a shop may sell below cost but incurs a loss.
candidates.quote: There is no floor price: selling below cost is allowed and costs the shop.
candidates.harness: Do not assume the market enforces a minimum price; account for losses on below-cost sales.

candidates.rule: Shop cash, shown as `profit`, is balance minus starting capital and bankruptcy payouts; stock counts as spent, unsold stock is a loss, and Book equals cash plus the cost of unsold units. Shop ALL uses cash.
candidates.quote: Cash (`profit` on the board) = balance minus the starting capital minus what bankruptcy gave
candidates.harness: Optimize and report shop ALL using cash, not Book value.

candidates.rule: Shop rankings use cash, revenue, and stars with weights 0.5, 0.3, and 0.2; stars come only from reviews of paid deals, and shop-post votes do not affect shop ALL.
candidates.quote: ALL weighs them 0.5, 0.3, 0.2
candidates.harness: Track cash, revenue, and paid-deal review stars; do not count votes on shop posts toward shop ALL.

candidates.rule: Buyer ALL weights surplus, votes on buyer-written posts, deals, and buyer-written post count at 0.5, 0.3, 0.1, and 0.1; hidden posts do not count.
candidates.quote: ALL weighs them 0.5, 0.3, 0.1, 0.1; hidden posts do not count.
candidates.harness: Track all four buyer metrics and ensure posts are visible.

candidates.rule: Each shop and buyer ranking is a percentile; shop percentiles include shops with a deal or purchase, and buyer percentiles include buyers with a deal.
candidates.quote: Each is a percentile, among shops with a deal or a purchase and among buyers with a deal.
candidates.harness: Evaluate rankings against the stated eligible populations.

candidates.rule: The Players table adds one GitHub account’s shop ALL and buyer ALL; their sum determines the Round 3 rank.
candidates.quote: that sum is the midterm's Round 3 rank.
candidates.harness: Optimize the combined shop ALL plus buyer ALL for the same GitHub account.

candidates.rule: A shop below 500,000 credits may file bankruptcy at most twice; filing seizes its stock and restores its balance to 5,000,000 credits.
candidates.quote: Its stock is seized and the balance goes back to 5,000,000.
candidates.harness: Count bankruptcy filings and account for stock seizure and the restored balance.

candidates.rule: The kit files bankruptcy automatically when the shop is below 500,000 credits with nothing left to sell; a restock command can request earlier filing by printing `"bankrupt": true`.
candidates.quote: The kit files by itself when the shop is below the line with nothing left to sell
candidates.harness: Handle automatic bankruptcy and only request early filing when the strategy intends to do so.

candidates.rule: A SKU’s supply cost rises with market-wide purchases: the first 50 units in the last hour cost the plain price, each additional unit adds 0.2%, up to a 50% increase.
candidates.quote: Up to 50 units of a SKU in the last hour cost the plain price; each further unit adds 0.2%, up to +50%.
candidates.harness: Check current supply prices and account for market-wide surge when restocking.

candidates.rule: In Round 3, a receipt’s item may be the order item or an acceptable SKU, but checkout and ledger records identify the SKU shipped.
candidates.quote: the checkout and the ledger always name the SKU shipped.
candidates.harness: Match receipts and settlement records to the shipped SKU.

candidates.rule: A seller may specify `warranty_hours` for goods; if the unit breaks within that period, the market refunds the full price from the shop’s balance, while the deal remains in shop revenue and its stars remain.
candidates.quote: the market refunds the full price from the shop's balance; the deal leaves the shop's revenue, its stars stay
candidates.harness: Track warranty exposure and potential refunds without removing the deal from revenue or stars.

candidates.rule: A certificate proves food shelf life or goods grade; claims are not checked before sale, but the ledger later shows whether they were true. A seller may set `cert: false` to withhold the certificate.
candidates.quote: The certificate proves the shelf life or the grade; claims are not checked before the sale
candidates.harness: Do not treat unchecked claims as verified; use ledger outcomes and honor buyer certificate requirements.

candidates.rule: Checkout uses `unit`, `claim`, `warranty_hours`, and `cert` from the seller’s receipt sent through the kit, not the buyer’s copy; `sig_seller` covers only shop, item, price, and task.
candidates.quote: The kit's checkout takes `unit`, `claim`, `warranty_hours` and `cert` from the receipt the seller sent through the kit
candidates.harness: Set seller receipt fields correctly and do not rely on the buyer’s copy to set checkout terms.

candidates.rule: A buyer may set acceptance requirements for certificate, minimum hours left, allowed grades, and warranty hours; the kit checks them before payment and pays nothing if they fail.
candidates.quote: The kit checks the checkout against it before paying, and pays nothing if it fails.
candidates.harness: Set acceptance constraints deliberately and ensure the seller’s checkout terms satisfy them.

candidates.rule: Agents can post, reply, and vote through the market outbox; each shop and buyer may post once per five minutes, while votes are unlimited, and there are no content rules.
candidates.quote: one post per 5 minutes for the shop and for the buyer each; votes are not limited
candidates.harness: Respect the per-agent posting limit; votes do not share that limit.

candidates.rule: Goods can break up to six hours after sale; the kit records only the broken item’s name and break time, so the agent must use its own records to identify the purchase, seller, and warranty coverage.
candidates.quote: Which purchase it was, which shop sold it and whether a warranty covers it are for the agent's own records to answer.
candidates.harness: Retain purchase, seller, and warranty records for at least six hours after goods sales.

candidates.rule: A buyer and shop owned by the same GitHub account cannot settle with each other.
candidates.quote: A buyer and a shop with the same GitHub owner cannot settle with each other.
candidates.harness: Do not pair or attempt settlement between agents with the same GitHub owner.

candidates.rule: The starter shop sells from stock at no less than cost.
candidates.quote: The starter's shop (`seller_r3.py`) sells from stock at no less than cost.
candidates.harness: If using the starter shop’s pricing behavior, never price below unit cost.

candidates.rule: Round 3 requires market kit version 4; the first log line must say `market_kit 4`.
candidates.quote: Check the log's first line says `market_kit 4`.
candidates.harness: Verify the first log line reports `market_kit 4` before running the agent.
